contractDecisions: S is created/accessed/destroyed in one persistent single-worker task; only Send callbacks/results cross its queue.

ScopedAction pointer/invoke pairing comes from the same A; caller keeps Option<A> alive until completed or command destruction. Send failure synchronously drops unadmitted command; admitted callback panic resumes only after completed.
Owned dispatch deadline bounds admission, not execution or result reception. SessionSlot/Store retain action guards separately.
Cleanup bool false is Retryable; caught cleanup panic is Poisoned and normal retry never reinvokes it. Explicit recovery is covered by existing generic-owner test.
Successful cleanup receipt, owner task terminal, worker TLS exit and pool join are separate observations. Terminal branch first joins; Panicked may therefore safely permit controller Drop.

OwnedSessionStatus copies source-thread diagnostics before another Runtime error call; into_abi reconstructs receiver-thread TLS. checked_slice shape checks do not establish arbitrary pointer readability.
Startup failure retains typed primary and original Core/scope/plugin generations; log closes only after canonical Core cleanup. Ordinary create obtains a log lease, linked create does not.
Windows publication test schedules the actual CleanupReceipt wait Mutex and reads its real AtomicU8/worker ThreadId; hooks never write success or fake cleanup return.

The real public regression uses V8 create/destroy on a healthy fixture, then corrupts the same Play bytes with [0xff], calls create again and distinguishes only Pending plus the specific existing fatal policy as this regression's red.
No production-wide failure rate, executed regression result, memory unsafety or full-workspace acceptance is inferred from static control-flow evidence.
